sysutils.c.reason: get_avail_memory issues DPMI 0500h with a 32-bit linear buffer address; the block arenas hold native records that carry 8-byte pointers.
divergences: get_avail_memory reports PORT_FREE_MEMORY (16 MiB) instead of querying DPMI; InitMemoryVariable therefore always takes its >= 3 MiB branch (normal mode, all sprites, backgrounds).
init_memory allocates PORT_ARENA_SCALE (2 on 64-bit hosts) times the requested capacity; block_malloc semantics are unchanged, only the out-of-memory threshold moves.

load.c.reason: Level/world loading reads 32-bit file words into pointer-typed fields and reads 132-byte DOS object images directly into obj_t; both depend on the 32-bit DOS layout.
divergences: Pointer-typed fields that receive a 32-bit file word (animations[].frames x3, ScrollDiffSprites, wldobj[].eta) are filled by port_fread_pointer_word (sign-extended word); the original sentinel tests and (s32) narrowing are unchanged.

Object instance records are decoded field by field from their DOS offsets (game/dos_records.c, offsets from docs/semantics/generated/semantics_dos.h); the four index words are rebound with the original (s16) narrowing. A malloc scratch array holds the index words; the game allocators are not touched.

load_world reads the BIOS tick byte at linear 0x46C four times while waiting for two tick edges (with the debug-register watch around it); the reads use port_bios_tick_byte(), the tick derived from the port clock. The watch itself is omitted (docs/port/PLATFORM_OPEN.md).

data/blk_215c.c.reason: DisplayBufferNormal is initialised with the VGA linear address 0xA0000.
divergences: DisplayBufferNormal points to the port display aperture (video/vga.c port_vga_aperture), the device that replaces VGA memory.

box.c.reason: Fire, CadreTrans and ClearBorder form draw-buffer addresses through a u32 round trip ((u8 *)((u32)draw_buffer + n)), which truncates a 64-bit pointer.
divergences: The four address computations use pointer arithmetic draw_buffer + n; for every in-range offset this is the same address the 32-bit u32 arithmetic produced. No other change.

map_ngawe.c.reason: INIT_GAME_MODE_NORMAL installs Copy_Plan0Diff_To_Buf behind island_copy_t, whose C parameter order (source, dest, pitch, height, width) differs from the routine's direct prototype (source, dest, width, height, pitch); the DOS register ABI made both views the same.
divergences: Copy_Plan0_To_Buf receives the adapter port_island_copy_plan0diff (video/lowlevel_adapters.c), which reorders the arguments for the same routine. Same pixels.

frame.c.reason: SWAP_BUFFERS calls Swap_And_Test_Joystick through frame.c's swap_func_t view, which lists EDI (destination) first; pcmain.c's view of the same pointer and the native routine take (source, destination).
divergences: The normal-mode joystick swap call passes (DrawBufferNormal, display_buffer): the same registers the DOS call loaded (ESI source, EDI destination).

jumelle.c.reason: PrepareJumelleZoom indexes its zoom table with u32 expressions (x - y*224, -y*224 - x, ...) that wrap to negative offsets in 32-bit arithmetic; on a 64-bit host the wrapped value is a +4 GiB offset.
divergences: The eight left[]/right[] index expressions are cast to s32: the same offsets the 32-bit program used. Found by the first native run (segmentation fault); this class is caught systematically by the i686 reference build (port/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

effect2.c.reason: The embedded draw descriptor starts at the native screen field; its DOS byte offset 0x3c precedes alignment padding on x64.
divergences: Select the screen field by member address; the descriptor contract and all drawing calculations are unchanged.

effect50350.c.reason: Two effect_segment_t records contain native texture pointers and outgrow the literal DOS allocation of 0x58 bytes.
divergences: Allocate two sizeof(effect_segment_t) records (0x58 bytes on i686); existing typed descriptor writes and native rasterizer contract remain unchanged.

effect633e0.c.reason: The effect_column_state_t allocation is the literal 0x30-byte DOS pointer-bearing layout.
divergences: Allocate sizeof(effect_column_state_t) (0x30 on i686); column tables, phases, and pixel calculations are unchanged.

effect6c3b0.c.reason: The radial effect state holds three pointers and outgrows the literal 0x20-byte DOS allocation.
divergences: Allocate sizeof(effect_state_6c_t) (0x20 on i686); the displacement map and update/draw order are unchanged.

effect6ec80.c.reason: The wave state uses a literal DOS allocation and vertex/local surface values store texture pointers in u32.
divergences: Allocate sizeof(effect_state_6e_t) (0xbc on i686).

Use u8 * for both surface declarations and assign texture pointers without u32 narrowing; projected words and rectangle bytes follow the native pointer in the existing descriptor contract. Vertex allocation already uses sizeof. All wave calculations are unchanged.

effecthelp.c.reason: The sphere state and items contain native pointers but allocate literal DOS record sizes.
divergences: Allocate sizeof(effect5_state_t) and count * sizeof(effect5_item_t) (0x3c and count * 52 on i686); sphere setup, interpolation, bounce/drop calculations, and embedded descriptor fields are unchanged.

blood.c.reason: DoEffectBloodOut compares two addresses after truncation to signed 32-bit values.
divergences: Compare the byte-height to the destination offset from the same frame origin. This preserves the original frame-origin test without pointer truncation or forming the potentially out-of-buffer row_start + height pointer. RNG order, all pixel writes, and synchronization are unchanged.

cdaudio.c.reason: DPMI register-block address truncation and 16:32 selector pointer overlays cannot represent native pointers.
divergences: sub_193f0 takes intptr_t and calls the correctly typed real-mode transport, preserving the register-block address on both architectures.

Eleven native pointer views are assigned from bounded port_cd_buffer offsets instead of writing offset:selector bytes into native pointer storage. Request bytes and all TOC/status/cue policy remain unchanged.

bss/bt.h.reason: bt.h opens #pragma pack(4) (never closed) before including the shared headers, so that Watcom places the central BSS with natural <= 4 alignment. With 8-byte pointers the BSS units then defined pointer-carrying types (mem_t, bande_t, ...) with a different layout than the code units (main_mem_world capacity aliased cdTime; the 288-row heat-haze Bande table of world 5 level 10 diverged).
divergences: No global pack(4): every BSS unit uses the native natural layout of the code units. temp_mem_entry_t keeps pack(4) between push/pop, exactly as sysutils_local.h declares it. The whole src/bss directory is compiled from the derived tree (unchanged copies) so that the units find this header.

hifi.c.reason: DOS bank headers are serialized 16-byte records; native pointers and the full data_6664.c config view have different layouts. Speech sets a DOS byte offset into the request flags.
divergences: No game calculations or service call order changed. Checksum and XOR process the same 2048 header bytes before field decoding and pointer binding.
Native data/config/request pointers replace padded DOS far-pointer views; full config member order matches the unchanged data_6664.c definition.
Speech request flags |= 0x100 replaces DOS byte-offset 0x29.

movie.c.reason: The DOS movie stack arrays overlap a pointer-bearing work record and use literal surface/timer offsets. The palette writer passes a surface address in u32.
divergences: Use native work/surface records and sizeof clears, named timer and sound_mode members, and typed pointer arguments. The 128-byte serialized work prefix remains identical (static assertions); no file-header decoding or calculation changes.
The palette writer context is a native surface pointer (ignored by both writers), avoiding address truncation.

Audited all literals, byte offsets and u32 indices: +6 chunk payload, 16/128-byte serialized prefixes, 320 stride and surface_offset remain file/pixel quantities. No subtracting u32 index or wrapped negative pointer offset occurs. Chunk semantics, signed8 run narrowing, unusual odd-byte control, pacing, palette/CD/input order and error codes are unchanged.
Optional RAYMAN_MOVIE_TRACE observations at entry/return, decoded frames and fade start; no calculations, call order between game/services or clock advances changed.

sub_3ABE4 calls port_record_asset (port/render/record.c) after its chunk loop: the decoded frame, read from the movie surface before it is paced and copied to the display, becomes an image operation of the native renderer; no game or decoder state changes.

display.c.reason: The conclusion caller declares playVideo as void(mem_t *,const char *,s16), while its actual definition takes a path string and u8 track and returns s32.
divergences: Declare the actual native playVideo signature and pass demo_video_mem as its char buffer, rather than a pointer to the array through mem_t *. The path address and track 21 are identical; return value remains ignored; no scene or service call order changes.

menu.c.reason: FonduOption's two in-place greyscale passes (the in-game and options menus' faded option rectangles) are C pixel loops inside a function called within its own unit, so the native renderer cannot observe them at link time.
divergences: Two calls to port_record_menu_grey (port/render/effect_capture.c), one immediately before each greyscale loop of FonduOption mode 1, record the pass for the native renderer; they read the rectangle and MenuPalette and change no game state.
